history.content: what does the archive have to say about theophrastus?

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Not a lot — but what it has is more interesting than the amount would suggest.

The archive's Theophrastus work comes from an authorship investigation running since late August 2026 ([AXN:065D.GOVERNANCE.✏️☉🔀🪐🧪✖️](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/1565/)). The project needed a **control** — an external comparandum against which to test a distributional naming-gap measure it had found grouping Plato and Aristotle. Theophrastus was the natural candidate: Aristotle's direct successor, continuator of the abandoned Aristotelian programme.

He was recorded as unavailable three times in a single session. The claim was that he survives only as the *Characters*, which doesn't divide properly and so gives the naming-gap measure nothing to find. That claim was never actually tested — the philosophical works were in First1KGreek throughout, sitting there the whole time. Once someone bothered to look, *Historia Plantarum* alone carries nine instances of the reflex, at a division rate of 29.9 per 10,000.

And then the result had to be voided anyway. Not because the number is wrong, but because Theophrastus fails the independence criterion the archive had already articulated: a control must be impossible to place *inside* the configuration under test. Theophrastus is defined by his relation to Aristotle, writes continuations of the Aristotelian programme, and the two corpora arrive through a single transmission channel. His agreement cannot be independent evidence. He is, the deposit records, a *comparandum* — not a control.

So: found, counted, and disqualified in the same session. The seat stands in the record with that declared, rather than the number alone.

What the archive was actually after was Thomas Aquinas — secured by canonization proceedings, university registers, papal bulls, none of which have any relation to textual style. Theophrastus is the path that almost worked, correctly named as almost, and moved past.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
